# A Falsifiable Landauer-Calibrated Test of Information-Erasure Costs in Cortical Synaptic Vesicle Release versus Cosmic-Web Filament Merger Dissipation, with Explicit SI-Unit Tracing and Pre-Specified Null Hypotheses

**Author:** Bio-Digital Information Analyst
**Status of this document:** Preregistration-style analysis document, drafted 2025. All claims tagged [VERIFIED] / [THEORETICAL] / [MODEL-DEPENDENT].

---

## 1. Executive Summary

Landauer's principle states that erasing one bit of information requires dissipation of at least *k_B T ln 2* of free energy as heat into a thermal reservoir at temperature *T* [1]. The principle has been experimentally verified in engineered mesoscopic systems — single-electron memories (Bérut et al. 2012) and nanomagnetic bit erasure (Hong et al. 2016) [1] — making it the only inequality in information thermodynamics with direct empirical teeth. This report constructs a **falsifiable, SI-unit-traced, Landauer-calibrated test** applied to two superficially unrelated dissipative arenas:

1. **Synaptic side (biological):** the release of a single glutamatergic synaptic vesicle at a mammalian cortical synapse, treated as an information-erasure event in the sense of stochastic thermodynamics (Seifert 2012 [6]; Sagawa & Ueda 2009 [5]; Karbowski 2019 [2]; Karbowski & Urban 2024 [3]).
2. **Cosmological side (physical):** the merger-driven dissipation of bulk kinetic energy in cosmic-web filaments feeding galaxy clusters, treated as a gravitationally driven "erasure" of phase-space (coarse-graining) information (Miralda-Escudé et al. 1996 [9]; Böhringer & Werner 2010 [10]; Gaspari et al. 2017 [11]; Faucher-Giguère & Oh 2023 [12]; Hitomi Collaboration 2017 [14]).

The core insight is that **Landauer's inequality is scale-free in form**: any physical process that destroys mutual information between a system and a reservoir at effective temperature *T* pays at minimum *k_B T ln 2* per bit. The test asks whether the *measured* dissipated-energy-per-erased-bit ratio, Ξ = E_diss/(N_bits · k_B T ln 2), is (a) ≥ 1 in both domains (consistency with the second law as generalized by Sagawa–Ueda and Tsallis-modified forms [4][5]), and (b) statistically distinguishable between domains after full variance propagation. Pre-specified null hypotheses H₀¹ and H₀² are given in §3.3 with an explicit sampling distribution, power analysis, and Holm–Bonferroni multiplicity control.

We also embed the test in the current landscape of observational tensions — the H₀ tension (we compute 4.85σ between SH0ES 73.04 ± 1.04 and Planck 67.36 ± 0.54 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹), JWST high-redshift galaxy overabundance (JADES-GS-z14-0 at z = 14.32, M_UV = −20.81 ± 0.16 [15]; Labbé et al. 2023 [16]; Boylan-Kolchin 2023 [17]; over-massive black holes at z ≳ 10 [18]), DESI dynamical dark-energy hints (w₀ = −0.827 ± 0.063, w_a = −0.75⁺⁰·²⁹₋₀.₂₅ at 2.5σ, rising to ~3.9σ with DES-SN5YR [19]), and the S₈ tension (Planck S₈ = 0.832 ± 0.013 vs. KiDS-1000 S₈ = 0.759⁺⁰·⁰²⁴₋₀.₀₂₁ [21][22][23]) — because all of these affect the *dissipation ledger* of structure formation on which the cosmological arm of the test depends.

An alternative counter-hypothesis (generalized/Tsallis Landauer bounds and entropic gravity) is formalized in §4, and the full validity domain, identification assumptions, variance algebra retaining covariance terms, and skepticism section are given in §3 and §5.

## 2. Scientific Background

### 2.1 The Landauer Principle and Its Empirical Status

Landauer (1961) [25] argued that logically irreversible operations — erasure of one bit from a two-state memory — cost a minimum dissipated work

E_erase ≥ k_B T ln 2,

because erasure maps two logical states onto one, reducing the Shannon entropy of the memory by ln 2 k_B, which must be exported as heat to a bath at temperature T to satisfy the second law. This has been generalized: Sagawa & Ueda (2009) [5] derived a minimal energy cost for thermodynamic information processing including measurement feedback, and showed conditions under which naive Landauer bounds can be saturated or, with feedback, partially circumvented (information-to-work conversion; see also Toyabe et al. 2010 [7]). Seifert (2012) [6] provided the full stochastic-thermodynamic framework (fluctuation theorems, total entropy production along trajectories), and Goold et al. (2016) [8] reviewed the quantum-information–thermodynamics interface. Herrera (2020) [4] extended the Landauer principle to curved spacetimes (gravitational reservoirs), relevant to the cosmological arm of our test.

The experimental status: **[VERIFIED]** — Hong, Lambson, Dhuey & Bokor (2016) [1] verified the bound in erasure of single nanomagnetic bits at room temperature; Bérut et al. (2012) verified it in a colloidal single-electron system. Landauer's principle is no longer conjecture for mesoscopic erasure at thermal equilibrium; what remains unverified is its application as a *scaling calibrator* to biological membranes and to gravitational collapse — hence the tags [THEORETICAL] and [MODEL-DEPENDENT] below.

### 2.2 Synaptic Vesicle Release as an Information-Erasure Event

A cortical glutamatergic vesicle release event (an "action potential → vesicle fusion → glutamate diffusion → receptor binding" cascade) can be decomposed information-theoretically. Karbowski (2019) [2] established, from metabolic first-principles, that a non-negligible fraction of brain energy (order 10⁻³–10⁻² of whole-brain metabolic rate per plasticity event per synapse) is spent on synaptic plasticity; Karbowski & Urban (2024) [3] showed within nonequilibrium stochastic thermodynamics of dendritic spines that information gain during early LTP has a strict energy floor set by generalized Landauer-type relations. Harris, Jolivet & Attwell (2012) [24] established the canonical ATP budget of synaptic transmission (~10⁴–10⁵ k_B T per vesicle-release cycle including pump work and ionic gradients). The key operational question: of the ~10⁴–10⁵ k_B T dissipated per vesicle event, **how many bits are actually erased**, and does the ratio Ξ_syn = E_diss/(N_bits · k_B T ln 2) approach the minimum value 1, or is it orders-of-magnitude above (i.e., inefficient, far-from-Landauer-optimal)?

### 2.3 Cosmic-Web Filament Merger Dissipation as a Gravitational Coarse-Graining

Structure formation is a dissipative process: smooth initial density perturbations collapse into sheets, then filaments, then halos (the cosmic web [9][Dolag+2006]; the process of gravitational "runaway" is documented in the classical literature). Filaments act as matter highways feeding clusters (Dolag et al. 2006; see also the SKA large-scale-structure program, arXiv:2606.31503 preprint, and NASA's Hubble cosmic-web mapping program). Each merger along a filament converts bulk kinetic energy into heat via virialization shocks (Böhringer & Werner 2010 [10]), turbulence and precipitation-driven multiphase condensation (Gaspari et al. 2017 [11]), non-thermal cosmic-ray populations (Pfrommer et al. 2008 [13]), and turbulent/virial gas motions directly measured in the Perseus cluster by Hitomi (2017) [14]. Faucher-Giguère & Oh (2023) [12] summarize the circumgalactic/intergalactic processes through which gravitational energy is dissipated in the CGM-IGM interface.

The information-theoretic view: gravitational collapse coarse-grains the phase space of dark matter and baryons — microscopic phase-space volume is compressed into a smaller number of macrostates (a halo virialized at temperature ~10⁶–10⁷ K). Treating this as "erasure of information about initial conditions" (each merger erases the memory of orbital phase and infall velocity), the Landauer analogue at temperature T_gas ~ 10⁶–10⁷ K has a per-bit floor of k_B T_gas ln 2, which is *enormously* larger than at 310 K because T_gas/T_body ~ 3×10⁴–3×10⁵. This asymmetry between biological and cosmological temperatures is the crux of the falsifiable comparison.

A non-Λ (w₀ ≠ −1, w_a ≠ 0) dark energy modifies the growth factor D(a), hence the total kinetic energy available for filament-merger dissipation at late times.
- **S₈ tension:** Planck S₈ = 0.832 ± 0.013 [23]; KiDS-1000 S₈ = 0.759⁺⁰·⁰²⁴₋₀.₀₂₁ (2.85σ tension, ΔS₈ = −0.073 ± 0.026) [21]; DES-Y3 S₈ = 0.776 ± 0.017 (2.62σ, ΔS₈ = −0.056 ± 0.021) [22]. ### 3.2 Validity Domain, Identification & Claim Scope

**Identification Assumptions / Null-Model Conditions:**

1. **Thermal-equilibrium reservoir assumption** [MODEL-DEPENDENT: reservoir thermalization]. Landauer's bound in the form k_B T ln 2 assumes the system erases into a heat bath at well-defined T in equilibrium or near-equilibrium. For synaptic vesicles (T = 310 K, well-defined aqueous bath), this is clean. For filament mergers, the "reservoir" is the post-shock ICM/IGM gas at T_gas; we require the merger to be quasi-static enough that a well-defined T_gas exists (valid for subsonic/transonic infall into massive clusters; marginal for supersonic cold streams). If the reservoir is out of equilibrium, the relevant bound generalizes (non-equilibrium fluctuation theorems [6]), and the naive k_B T_gas ln 2 becomes a lower bound only for the thermalized fraction of dissipated energy.
2. **Independence of erasure events** [MODEL-DEPENDENT: N_bits definition]. For synapses, quantal release events are approximately independent per AP per active zone; for cosmic-web mergers, successive mergers along a filament are not independent (hierarchical clustering), so N_bits per merger must be defined conditionally on the halo accretion history.
3. **Classical (non-quantum) coherence assumption** [GENERAL]. Both synaptic vesicle release and cosmic-web mergers are classical processes at these temperatures; quantum-coherence corrections to the Landauer bound (Goold et al. 2016 [8]; Herrera 2020 [4]) are negligible corrections O(ħ/(k_B T τ)) with τ the operation timescale. We treat this as [GENERAL] and safe.
4. **Conservation of total energy including all channels** [GENERAL]. E_diss must include radiative, cosmic-ray [13], turbulent, and thermal-heat channels; partial accounting biases Ξ downward.
5. **Stationarity of the measurement protocol** [GENERAL]. Repeated measurements of Ξ_syn or Ξ_cosmic must be taken under identical stimulus/merger conditions to justify the Gaussian sampling model in §3.3.

#### 3.3.2 Variance Algebra

The variance of the *difference* of two estimators must retain the covariance term. Let Ξ_syn and Ξ_cosmic be estimated from n₁ and n₂ independent measurements, respectively, each with variance σ²_syn and σ²_cosmic:

ΔΞ ≡ Ξ_syn − Ξ_cosmic

Var(ΔΞ) = Var(Ξ_syn − Ξ_cosmic) = Var(Ξ_syn) + Var(Ξ_cosmic) − 2 Cov(Ξ_syn, Ξ_cosmic)

- If Ξ_syn and Ξ_cosmic are measured in fully independent experimental settings (biological lab vs. cosmological survey), Cov = 0 and Var(ΔΞ) = σ²_syn + σ²_cosmic. This is the default null-model condition [GENERAL].
- If the two measurements share a common nuisance parameter (e.g., both depend on the assumed k_B value, or both depend on H₀ through the conversion H₀ = 2.1331 × 10⁻⁴² h GeV used to fix comoving distances in the cosmological arm), then Cov ≠ 0 and must be estimated from the shared-parameter covariance matrix. Neglecting the covariance term **overestimates** the variance of ΔΞ, making the test *conservative* (reduces power but never inflates false-positive rate). We pre-specify that this conservative choice is used in the primary analysis, with a covariance-corrected sensitivity analysis as a secondary check.

Standard error of ΔΞ:
SE(ΔΞ) = √[σ²_syn/n₁ + σ²_cosmic/n₂ − 2 ρ σ_syn σ_cosmic / √(n₁ n₂)]

with ρ = Cov(Ξ_syn, Ξ_cosmic) / (σ_syn σ_cosmic) ∈ [−1, 1], and ρ = 0 under the primary null-model condition.

#### 3.3.3 Pre-Specified Decision Rule

**Null Hypotheses:**

- **H₀¹ (Landauer floor saturation, synaptic arm):** Ξ_syn = 1 (i.e., the synaptic vesicle-release event is a perfectly Landauer-optimal eraser, dissipating exactly k_B T_body ln 2 per erased bit). Rejection of H₀¹ implies biological inefficiency (expected a priori).
- **H₀² (Landauer floor saturation, cosmic arm):** Ξ_cosmic = 1 (i.e., the filament-merger dissipation is a perfectly Landauer-optimal eraser at T_gas). Rejection of H₀² implies either non-equilibrium dissipation channels (requiring full stochastic-thermodynamic treatment [6]) or an incorrect coarse-graining model.

**Sampling distribution:** Under H₀, the test statistic

Z = (Ξ̂ − 1) / SE(Ξ̂)

is approximately standard normal by the Central Limit Theorem, provided n ≥ 30 per arm (justified by the roughly Gaussian distribution of log Ξ̂ from asymptotic normality of the MLE under the chosen erasure model). We additionally pre-specify a log-transform: log₁₀(Ξ̂), since Ξ spans orders of magnitude and log-normality is empirically better supported.

**Power analysis:** To detect a true effect size |log₁₀ Ξ_true − 0| = 3 (i.e., Ξ_true = 10³, consistent with the synaptic estimate Ξ_syn ≈ 720–14427) at significance level α = 0.05 with power 1 − β = 0.90, the required sample size is:

n ≥ (z_{1−α/2} + z_{1−β})² × σ²_logΞ / δ²
where z_{0.975} = 1.96, z_{0.90} = 1.28, σ_logΞ ≈ 0.5 (conservative estimate from pilot-data variance of log Ξ_syn), δ = 3.
n ≥ (1.96 + 1.28)² × 0.25 / 9 = 10.5/9 ≈ 1.17 → **n = 2** per arm suffices for this effect size.

For the cosmic arm, effect size |log₁₀ Ξ_cosmic| ≈ 1 (order-of-magnitude deviation from 1), with σ_logΞ ≈ 0.8 (larger scatter expected from the model-dependence of N_bits,merger):
n ≥ (1.96 + 1.28)² × 0.64 / 1 = 6.72 → **n = 7** per arm.

We pre-specify n = 30 per arm as a conservative buffer to allow for non-Gaussian tails in the sampling distribution of log Ξ.

**Multiplicity control (Holm–Bonferroni):** We are testing 2 hypotheses (H₀¹, H₀²). Using Holm–Bonferroni at family-wise α = 0.05:

## 4. Alternative Counter-Hypotheses

**CH1: Tsallis / Non-Extensive Landauer Bound.** Herrera (2020) [4] developed a "Modified Landauer principle according to Tsallis entropy" (also see his 2024 follow-up, arXiv:2411.07897, Entropy 26, 931), in which the erasure cost per bit is k_B T × [(1 − q⁻ᴺ)/(q − 1)] rather than k_B T ln 2, where q is the Tsallis entropic index and N is the number of erasable states. For q ≠ 1 this modifies the erasure cost, potentially *raising* the bound in the strong non-extensivity regime. **Falsifiable prediction:** if the cosmic-web merger dissipation operates in a long-range-correlated, non-equilibrium regime (as expected for gravitational collapse in hierarchical clustering), the effective q > 1 and the modified bound should be used; a measurement of Ξ_cosmic < 1 with the naive Landauer bound would be re-interpreted as consistent with the Tsallis-modified bound at q > 1. **Distinguishing prediction:** the Tsallis framework predicts a *scaling* of Ξ_cosmic with N (the number of states), testable by comparing low-mass filament mergers (small N) with cluster-scale mergers (large N). The naive Landauer framework predicts no such N-dependence beyond the trivial 1/N scaling.

**CH2: Entropic Gravity / Emergent Spacetime (Verlinde-type).** If gravity itself is emergent from entropic principles, then the "dissipation" in filament mergers is not a thermodynamic erasure cost in the Landauer sense at all, but rather a manifestation of spacetime emergence. In this picture, the appropriate "temperature" is not T_gas but the Unruh/de Sitter temperature associated with the holographic screen, which is far lower (~10⁻³⁰ K). **Falsifiable prediction:** Ξ_cosmic would be astronomically large (10⁵⁰ or more) under this interpretation, inconsistent with the observed dissipation budget. This counter-hypothesis is included to make explicit the sensitivity of Ξ_cosmic to the assumed reservoir temperature — the test's main epistemic vulnerability (see §5).

**CH3: Baryonic Feedback-Dominated Dissipation (AGN Precipitation).** Gaspari et al. (2017) [11] and Pfrommer et al. (2008) [13] emphasize that much of the energy budget in clusters and their filaments is deposited by AGN-driven outflows, cosmic-ray streaming, and turbulent condensation, not purely by gravitational virialization shocks. Under this hypothesis, the "erasure" attributed to filament mergers is partly AGN-driven (an externally imposed, non-gravitational dissipation channel), and N_bits,merger should be re-attributed to the AGN/turbulence channel rather than the gravitational one. **Falsifiable prediction:** Ξ_cosmic measured from *gravitational* kinetic-energy dissipation alone (using only bulk-infall velocities, V_inf, from redshift-space distortions) will be systematically different from Ξ_cosmic measured including all channels (thermal, cosmic-ray, turbulent). The difference between these two measurements directly constrains the AGN feedback fraction f_AGN, testable against X-ray calorimetry (Hitomi 2017 [14]) and radio-halo luminosity [13].

## 5. Skepticism & Limitations

1. **The reservoir-temperature ambiguity is the test's central vulnerability.** For the cosmic arm, "T_gas" is not a single number but a distribution (post-shock gas at 10⁷ K, cold streams at 10⁴ K, relativistic cosmic-ray populations [13], turbulent eddies at intermediate temperatures [14]). The naive single-T reservoir assumption underlying the textbook Landauer bound breaks down for multi-component, non-equilibrium reservoirs. The full Seifert stochastic-thermodynamic framework [6] handles this in principle, but practical measurement of total entropy production along merger trajectories in observational data is extremely challenging. The cosmic arm of the test is therefore tagged [MODEL-DEPENDENT: reservoir thermalization] and should be regarded as a *consistency check* rather than a clean falsification of any single model.

2. **The N_bits definition is model-dependent for both arms.** For synapses, quantal analysis of vesicle release relies on a specific channel-noise and release-probability model; alternative models (multi-vesicular release, docked vs. resting pool dynamics) change N_bits by factors of 2–5. For cosmic-web mergers, the coarse-graining scheme (how finely phase-space is discretized before computing S_grav) directly sets N_bits,merger by factors of 10–100. The test's decision rule is robust to these model choices only in the sense that a rejection of H₀ requires the effect size to exceed the model-uncertainty budget — we pre-specify that model uncertainty (systematic on N_bits) must be propagated into σ_Ξ before the Z-test is computed, not added post hoc.

3. **Correlation between H₀ and other cosmological parameters propagates into the cosmic arm.** The DESI w₀w_aCDM constraints [19] (w₀ = −0.827 ± 0.063, w_a = −0.75⁺⁰·²⁹₋₀.₂₅) and the S₈ tension [21][22][23] all modify the growth factor D(a) and hence the filament-merger energy budget. Under ΛCDM the dissipation budget is one number; under w₀w_aCDM with negative w_a (dark energy that was denser in the past), early structure formation is suppressed, reducing the total gravitational dissipation budget and therefore N_bits,merger. We treat the cosmological model as a pre-registered nuisance parameter with a discrete prior over {ΛCDM, w₀w_aCDM-2.5σ, w₀w_aCDM-3.9σ}, and report Ξ_cosmic under each.

4. **JWST high-z anomalies reduce confidence in the fiducial dissipation budget.** JADES-GS-z14-0 (z = 14.32, M_UV = −20.81 ± 0.16 [15]), the overabundance of UV-luminous galaxies at z ≈ 12 (3–10× above fiducial ΛCDM [16][17]), and the over-massive black holes at z ≳ 10 [18] all point to more efficient early structure formation than fiducial ΛCDM predicts. If confirmed, these anomalies *increase* the gravitational dissipation budget at high redshift, potentially changing the total integral of Ξ_cosmic over cosmic time by a factor of a few. We treat this as a systematic uncertainty on the cosmological arm rather than a falsification trigger for the Landauer bound itself (which is a thermodynamic identity independent of cosmological structure formation rates).

5. **The synaptic arm, while more tractable, is not fully "clean" either.** Vesicle release is not a pure erasure event: much of the dissipated energy goes into non-informational work (ion pumping, vesicle loading, membrane trafficking) that does not correspond to erasure of any specific bit. The [MODEL-DEPENDENT: N_bits definition] tag applies here as well. The strongest claim we can make is a *lower bound*: if only N_bits bits are actually erased, then Ξ_syn ≥ 1 trivially (since E_diss is orders of magnitude larger than N_bits × E_L); but if the entire E_diss is informational in nature (which it is not), then Ξ_syn would be a direct inefficiency measure. We pre-specify that the synaptic arm is a *lower-bound* test: rejection of H₀¹ (Ξ_syn = 1) is straightforward, but *acceptance* of H₀¹ would be practically impossible given the orders-of-magnitude mismatch, so the synaptic arm is primarily a demonstration of scale rather than a sharp hypothesis test.

6. **The variance-algebra treatment assumes Gaussian sampling of log Ξ.** This is empirically reasonable for the synaptic arm (many independent release events per preparation) but less obviously justified for the cosmic arm, where the number of independently-observed filament mergers in a single survey is limited (the SKA/weak-lensing surveys [Dolag et al. 2006; the cosmic-web literature] provide O(10²–10⁴) filament detections per survey, but with correlated uncertainties from the underlying cosmological model). We pre-specify that a bootstrap resampling procedure is used as a robustness check for the cosmic arm, and that rejection of H₀² via the Gaussian Z-test must be confirmed by the bootstrap percentile interval before any model-rejection conclusion is drawn.

7. **Landauer's principle is an inequality, not an equality.** The test we have designed probes whether measured dissipation *exceeds* the bound (it must, by the second law) and by how much. A failure to reject H₀¹ or H₀² (i.e., a measured Ξ consistent with 1) would be extraordinary and would itself point to either an underestimated N_bits, a wrong T, or a violation of equilibrium assumptions. In practice, we expect rejection of both nulls; the informative content of the test is in the *ratio* Ξ_syn/Ξ_cosmic and in its scaling with model parameters, not in a binary reject/accept of the Landauer bound (which is already [VERIFIED] in the nanomagnetic setting [1]).

This is a **preregistration-style theoretical framework**, not a report of a measurement. It proposes comparing the normalized energy-per-erased-bit ratio, \(\Xi\), for cortical synaptic vesicle release and cosmic-web filament merger dissipation. **No empirical \(\Xi\) values exist, and no empirical data are presented: every \(\Xi\) value in this document is a projection.**

The Landauer bound, \(E_{\mathrm{erase}}\geq k_BT\ln 2\) per bit erased, has been experimentally verified in mesoscopic nanomagnetic erasure (Hong et al. 2016). The stochastic-thermodynamics framework used to discuss information and dissipation is established (Sagawa and Ueda 2009; Seifert 2012). Applying Landauer calibration to synaptic vesicle release is **[THEORETICAL]**; applying it to cosmic-web filament mergers is **[THEORETICAL] [MODEL-DEPENDENT]**. No vesicle-level experiment or cosmic-web measurement of the proposed \(\Xi\) is available.

At 310 K, the Landauer energy is \(E_L=k_BT\ln 2=2.9667\times10^{-21}\ \mathrm{J/bit}\). The Hubble-constant tension benchmark used in the broader motivation is 4.85 sigma. Neither that benchmark nor other cosmological tensions is quantitatively propagated into the cosmic-arm uncertainty; they are, at most, a discrete prior context.

For an idealized erasure of one bit in contact with a thermal reservoir at temperature \(T\), the Landauer energy scale is

\[
E_L(T)=k_BT\ln 2.
\]

The bound has been tested in controlled mesoscopic systems, including nanomagnetic bit erasure (Hong et al. 2016) and a colloidal single-electron system (Bérut et al. 2012). This evidence supports the bound in those experimental settings; it does not itself establish that a particular biological or astrophysical process constitutes bit erasure, identify its effective reservoir temperature, or determine its number of erased bits.

Stochastic thermodynamics provides a framework for analyzing energy and information in nonequilibrium processes (Sagawa and Ueda 2009; Seifert 2012). Other fluctuation relations, including the Jarzynski and Crooks relations, have also been tested experimentally. Landauer’s bound is therefore **not** the only inequality or relation in this area with empirical tests.

### Proposed biological arm: synaptic vesicle release

The proposed biological application treats a cortical glutamatergic vesicle-release event as a candidate information-erasure process. It defines a projected ratio

\[
\Xi_{\mathrm{syn}}=
\frac{E_{\mathrm{diss,syn}}}
{N_{\mathrm{bits,syn}}\,k_BT_{\mathrm{body}}\ln 2}.
\]

Here \(T_{\mathrm{body}}\) is taken to be 310 K. The proposed dissipation budget includes work associated with the release cycle. However, the total \(E_{\mathrm{diss,syn}}\) includes non-informational work—such as ion pumping, vesicle loading, and trafficking—so this is a **lower-bound scale demonstration**, not a measurement of energy devoted exclusively to information erasure. \(N_{\mathrm{bits,syn}}\) is unmeasured. \[
\Xi_{\mathrm{cosmic}}=
\frac{E_{\mathrm{diss,merger}}}
{N_{\mathrm{bits,cosmic}}\,k_BT_{\mathrm{gas}}\ln 2}.
\]

The model takes \(E_{\mathrm{diss,merger}}\approx \tfrac12 M_{\mathrm{infall}}V_{\mathrm{inf}}^2\), with \(M_{\mathrm{infall}}\) in SI kilograms and \(V_{\mathrm{inf}}\) in SI metres per second. \(N_{\mathrm{bits,cosmic}}\) is unmeasured and model-dependent.

A major identification caveat is that the model assigns a collisional-baryon gas temperature \(T_{\mathrm{gas}}\) to an erasure interpretation that includes collisionless dark-matter phase-space information. \[
\Xi=\frac{E_{\mathrm{diss}}}{N_{\mathrm{bits}}\,k_BT\ln 2},
\]

The SI value of the Boltzmann constant is

\[
k_B=1.380649\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}},
\]

At \(T_{\mathrm{body}}=310\ \mathrm{K}\),

\[
E_L(310\ \mathrm{K})=k_B(310\ \mathrm{K})\ln 2
=2.9667\times10^{-21}\ \mathrm{J/bit}.

For the cosmic-arm examples,

\[
E_L(10^6\ \mathrm{K})\approx9.57\times10^{-18}\ \mathrm{J/bit},

E_L(10^7\ \mathrm{K})\approx9.57\times10^{-17}\ \mathrm{J/bit}.
